newsitem.title: USA: Euro to play key role as reserve currency - Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: Euro to play key role as reserve currency - Rexrodt.

text.p: The planned common European currency will lessen the dollar's role as the world's dominant reserve currency, German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Tuesday.

European economic and monetary union, due to start in January 1999, will create a single currency sphere that will rival the dollar's in scale, he said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery at the European Institute.
"I do not believe that in the foreseeable future the dollar's role as the dominant currency for investors and international trade will be put in question," Rexrodt said.
"(But) in the long term, a stable euro will lower the dollar's burdens as a reserve currency and contribute to the stability of the world currency system," he said.

Rexrodt said he believed EMU would start on schedule with a large number of European countries participating. He repeated the government's forecasts that German economic growth will rebound to 2.5 percent this year, helping it meet the fiscal criteria to qualify for EMU.
Europe's efforts to meet the EMU goals have already had beneficial effects by lowering inflation and interest rates, he said.
